notes.subject: Drink
notes.rationale: The father addresses the son with a direct imperative.

notes.subject: to the son
notes.rationale: Second-masculine-singular address throughout: your cistern, your well.

notes.subject: cistern / well
notes.rationale: The water imagery is a metaphor for marital fidelity — the wife's body and the husband's sexuality; the Hebrew keeps the plain picture.

notes.subject: <streams>
notes.rationale: נֹזְלִים is a participle 'flowing ones' used as a noun; English needs a supplied noun head.

translation: Drink water from your own cistern, and flowing <streams> from the midst of your own well.
